sections.h2: Where is the McMinn County Register of Deeds, and what does the office do?
sections.html:
The register's office sits on the main floor of the courthouse at 6 East Madison Avenue in Athens, TN 37303, and the phone is (423) 745-1232. Cheryl Ingram holds the elected post, and the posted hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Staff record real estate conveyances, deeds of trust, leases and other instruments, and they issue certified copies of what is on file. The register is chosen by voters countywide every four years. If you are selling a house in McMinn County, the deed that moves title to your buyer ends up on this counter, usually delivered by a title company or attorney.

The county's register page says the office takes debit and credit cards, except American Express. Ask the staff what the total will be before you send a deed with extra pages, because the county's fee schedule is not printed on that page.

sections.h2: What does McMinn County look like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
McMinn County was created in 1819 and named for Joseph McMinn, a governor of Tennessee. Athens is the county seat and largest city. Etowah, Niota and Sweetwater are the other cities, and Calhoun and Englewood are towns. Most of the county lies in the Ridge and Valley section of the Appalachians, and the Hiwassee River marks the line with Bradley County to the southwest.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page shows a July 2025 population estimate of 57,404, up 7.8% from the 2020 base. The county has 24,424 housing units on 430 square miles of land, which works out to about 124 people per square mile. Median household income is $61,470, and the median gross rent is $803 a month.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $211,800.
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 75.8%.
  • Residents aged 65 or older: 21.1%.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 125.

Public schools come from three systems. McMinn County Schools runs the two high schools, while Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District cover grades K through 8 in their own areas. Tennessee Wesleyan University is in Athens.

sections.h2: How much is the tax on recording a deed in McMinn County?
sections.html:
Tennessee levies a realty transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 and a mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 of debt, with the first $2,000 of debt exempt. The register collects both when the document is recorded, and the state's recordation tax manual says the buyer named on the deed owes the transfer tax.

Tennessee recordation tax rates collected at the McMinn County register
TaxRateWho pays by default
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of price or valueGrantee (buyer)
Mortgage (indebtedness) tax$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exemptBorrower
Receipt fee for the taxUp to $1 per receiptFiler

Source: Tennessee Department of Revenue rate page and recordation tax manual. A purchase contract can move these costs, so read it before closing.

Here is a worked example at the Census median. A $211,800 sale is 2,118 hundreds, and 2,118 times $0.37 comes to $783.66 in transfer tax. A buyer financing $170,000 would owe mortgage tax on $168,000, or 1,680 hundreds at $0.115, which is $193.20. The tax base is the greater of the price paid or the property's value.

sections.h2: What does the McMinn County register require before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The county publishes a one-page checklist titled Requirements to Record Documents. A deed missing a listed item is likely to be returned at the counter, so go through it with your closing agent.

  • The name and address of whoever prepared the document, matching any return envelope you enclose.
  • The grantee's name and address, plus the name and address where tax bills should go.
  • The map and parcel number, a legal description, and the source of title by book and page.
  • Signatures of the proper parties, each notarized, with the notary's name, seal and date on the acknowledgment.
  • The oath of consideration, sworn before the register or a notary, stating the price or the value of the property, whichever is greater.
  • For any document tied to debt, the sentence "Maximum principal indebtedness for TN tax recording purposes is $___."

Corrected documents must be signed and acknowledged again unless a scrivener's affidavit is attached. The checklist also says documents sent without a stamped, self-addressed return envelope may be destroyed 90 days after recording, so include one if you want the original back.

sections.h2: Which McMinn County transfers owe no realty transfer tax?
sections.html:
The state manual lists several transfers that skip the $0.37 tax, and a few of them come up in family and estate sales. An oath is not needed on an exempt transfer.

  • Transfers of a leasehold estate.
  • A spouse conveying to the other spouse when a tenancy by the entirety is created or ended.
  • A deed signed by an executor to carry out a gift in a will.
  • Domestic decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing spouses.
  • Transfers into or out of a revocable living trust by the same owner or that owner's spouse.
  • Transfers to or from a government body.

A quitclaim deed is taxed on the consideration given, yet the state taxes fair market value when its wording shows an intent to pass the property itself, such as "in fee simple." The Department of Revenue also reviews deeds from random counties and date ranges, comparing the oath value with the assessor's figure and sending an inquiry letter when they differ. An unusually low stated price on a McMinn County deed can draw that letter.

sections.h2: How do you search records or e-record documents in McMinn County?
sections.html:
The register accepts electronic recordings through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company (CSC) and eRecording Partners Network (EPN). Most closings use one of these, so your title company will handle the submission.

For searching, the county points researchers to US Title Search Network, which charges per search or a monthly fee. If that service gives you trouble, the register's page lists Progress Inc. at 1 (800) 394-7477. Assessor data is separate: the county's Assessor of Property, Keith Price, at (423) 745-2743, keeps parcel maps and property cards, and the state's assessment website lets you look up map and parcel numbers that every conveyance needs.

If you inherited a McMinn County house and need to sell, ask the register how the executor's deed should be worded, and ask the probate clerk for proof of authority.

sections.h2: Who bills the property tax when a McMinn County house sells?
sections.html:
The McMinn County Trustee collects county property tax at the courthouse, 6 East Madison Avenue, phone (423) 745-1291. Current-year taxes are payable from October 1 through the last day of February, and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., plus Saturday mornings in February.

The Trustee also takes applications for the state's Tax Relief Program for elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled veterans. The county page says applications must be finished no later than 35 days after the February 28 payment deadline. Relief reimburses part of a paid tax bill, so it does not remove the bill.

Ask your title company how the current year's tax will be split at closing. Ask the Trustee for a payoff figure for your parcel before the closing date, and ask the assessor if the owner name or mailing address on the roll needs correcting.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in McMinn County?
faqs.a: The McMinn County Register of Deeds, at 6 East Madison Avenue in Athens, records it. The office is in the courthouse, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the phone is (423) 745-1232. Title companies usually submit by e-recording.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a McMinn County home sale?
faqs.a: It is $0.37 per $100 of the greater of price or value, collected by the register at recording. On a $211,800 home, the Census median for the county, that is $783.66. The buyer named on the deed owes it unless the contract says otherwise.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed electronically in McMinn County?
faqs.a: Yes. The register accepts e-recordings through Simplifile, CSC and eRecording Partners Network. Individuals without an account normally rely on their title company or attorney to submit the deed.

faqs.q: Does an inherited house in McMinn County owe transfer tax when sold?
faqs.a: A deed an executor signs to carry out a will gift is exempt from the realty transfer tax, but a later sale to a buyer is taxed at the normal rate. Ask the register to confirm how each deed in the chain will be treated.

faqs.q: Where do I pay McMinn County property tax before closing?
faqs.a: Pay the McMinn County Trustee at the courthouse in Athens or by the methods the office lists. Call (423) 745-1291 for a payoff figure. County taxes are due October 1 through the last day of February.
